senses.sense_definition: A device that measures and records physiological responses to detect if someone is lying.

examples.text: The suspect was asked to take a <w>polygraph</w> test to prove his innocence.
The results of the <w>polygraph</w> were inconclusive during the criminal investigation.

senses.sense_definition: A collection of various literary works by one or more authors.

examples.text: The library holds a rare <w>polygraph</w> containing essays from several different centuries.
Scholars often study this <w>polygraph</w> to understand the diverse themes of the era.

senses.sense_definition: An author who writes extensively on many different subjects.

examples.text: Known as a true <w>polygraph</w>, the writer published books on history, science, and poetry.
The prolific <w>polygraph</w> contributed hundreds of articles to the encyclopedia.

senses.sense_definition: A group of letters treated as a single unit in writing or linguistics.

examples.text: In this specific orthographic system, the <w>polygraph</w> represents a single complex sound.
Linguists analyze how each <w>polygraph</w> functions within the structure of the ancient text.

senses.sense_definition: A mechanical instrument used for creating multiple copies of a document.

examples.text: Before the invention of the printer, a <w>polygraph</w> was used to duplicate handwritten letters.
The antique <w>polygraph</w> sits on display in the museum of early office technology.

traits.comment: Refers to historical mechanical copying devices.

senses.sense_definition: To perform a lie detector test on someone.

examples.text: The police decided to <w>polygraph</w> every employee who had access to the vault.
They will <w>polygraph</w> the witness to verify the details of the statement.
